data.hypothesis: The serial path should avoid OpenMP team startup when threads<=1. For small effective teams (up to 4), static row assignment should keep scheduling overhead low; for larger teams such as 40, dynamic one-row chunks may better balance variation in per-ray BVH work. Rows give each pixel exactly one writer, while the ray calculation and both output writes stay unchanged. The controller must measure the tradeoff; no candidate speedup is assumed.
data.notes: Only the supplied serial baseline is measured: valid on all 6 correctness cases, with times 0.233650247, 0.233697199, and 0.233712945 s (mean 0.233686797 s; range 0.000062697 s, about 0.0268% of the mean). No candidate result or speedup is available yet. The T1 catalog has no earlier trials or source diversity, so there are no prior T1 policies to compare against. The proposed policy tests static scheduling at 4 and dynamic scheduling at larger teams, including 40; controller measurements should report the dispersion for those runs.
transformations: Retain the existing serial rendering path for threads<=1 (and when the effective team is one).
Add OpenMP row parallelism with num_threads capped by both threads and image height; each worker writes its assigned rows and both output arrays.
Use static row scheduling for effective teams of up to 4 and dynamic one-row scheduling for larger teams to test the scheduling-overhead/load-balance tradeoff.
